newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end higher after nervous day.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end higher after nervous day.

text.p: Italian shares ended an uncertain see-saw trading day on Thursday when the market overcame worries about the government's apparent wavering committment to tough financial discipline and Wall Street's lower opening.

Stocks dipped into negative territory by the middle of the day after a firmer start, but a good performance from individual shares such as Fiat, ENI and STET helped push the Mib30 index to finish on the day's highs, up 1.07 percent at 18,785.
"There were some political nerves around today, but in the end the mood picked up," said one share trader.
All-share Mibtel index ended up 0.78 percent at 12,587.

Dealers said the weakness was caused by doubts over the government's determination to introduce a 1997 mini-budget or bringing forward the 1998 budget into this year, and also concern over its committment towards pension reform.
The market also detected a sense of uncertainty as the PDS, the largest party in the government coalition, was seen as less willing to accept more cuts in government spending.

Nevertheless, leading blue chips led the recovery with ENI up 1.02 percent at 9,038 lire, Fiat 0.8 percent firmer at 5,318 lire, Edison 1.82 percent higher at 9,721 lire and telecoms holding STET 2.25 percent firmer at 8,334 lire.

STET gained after dealers considered a favourable share swap between STET and Telecom Italia after Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglo Ciampi said Wednesday that the Treasury's stake in the merged group would drop below 50 percent.

Food group Parmalat continued to slip, off 1.68 percent at 2,453 lire, despite its denial of market rumours over capital operations and 1996 results on Wednesday which pushed it shares down 7.25 percent.
Mediaset shares recovered, up 0.34 percent at 7,284 lire, after Canal Plus said late Wednesday it intended to maintain its shareholding in Mediaset.
